generated.title: Pervasive use of first-person singular "I"
generated.description: The guidelines explicitly state to avoid "I." The proposal uses "I" as the subject 24 or more times across the Abstract, Objectives, and Schedule sections. The student should restructure sentences to use "the thesis," "this work," "the platform," or the system itself as the active subject (e.g., "This thesis develops a self-service platform…", "The platform models resources as a tree…", "Each iteration delivers…"). The AI Transparency Statement is the one context where first person is arguably unavoidable, but even there, passive or impersonal constructions are preferable.

locations.section: Abstract
locations.quote: In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which every grant carries an expiry date from the moment somebody requests it.

locations.section: Abstract
locations.quote: **I evaluate** the platform at the chair on correctness, administrative effort, and extensibility.

locations.section: Objective
locations.quote: In this thesis, **I develop** a self-service platform on which requesters ask for time-limited access, maintainers decide, and access ends on its own.

locations.section: Objective
locations.quote: Following the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, **I pursue** four objectives:

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I model** the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to leaves bound to target systems.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I implement** the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors, whose credentials administrators configure at runtime.

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I reach** this objective when the webhook connector, written after I freeze the framework, needs one new class and one registry entry.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: **I evaluate** correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: **I reach** this objective when each access disappears after expiry and, in a second run with the workflow engine disabled on purpose, the drift check reports the remaining SSH membership.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: Keycloak gates its workflow API on a realm-wide administrative role that maintainers must not hold, so **I split** each decision into a review step, in which the maintainer records a decision without changing Keycloak, and a grant step, in which an administrator sets membership and expiry together.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: **I reach** this objective when administrators perform fewer manual actions and requesters wait less than in the current process.

locations.section: 4.4 Automate the Recertification of Active Grants
locations.quote: **I reach** this objective when the platform answers, for any grant, who requested it and why, who reviewed and granted it, when it ended, and who confirmed it since.

locations.section: Schedule
locations.quote: **I divide** the work into six iterations of four weeks, each ending with a vertically integrated increment.

locations.section: Schedule
locations.quote: **I reserve** the final two weeks, from 18 to 31 March 2027, as buffer for features that slip from earlier iterations.

locations.section: Schedule
locations.quote: Iteration 1, 1–28 October (Objective 1): **I deliver** the Keycloak realm with OpenID Connect login, SSH key self-service, and the resource tree with inherited maintainers.
